text: DSH Host File Explorer 是面向 DSH 网页端的宿主机文件浏览插件，会在左侧栏加入文件面板，并通过 Host/Client Remote 服务读取 Harness 所在机器的文件系统。用户可以查看目录、路径、文件大小和修改时间，预览文本与图片，下载文件、上传文件并创建子目录；界面提供多种语言。适合需要从 DSH 网页界面查看或整理运行 Harness 的机器文件的用户。无需额外 API 密钥或外部服务；操作由 Harness 进程在本机执行。

DSH Host File Explorer adds a sidebar panel for browsing the Harness machine's files. It lists directories, previews text and images, transfers files, and creates folders through a Remote service. Its web UI suits users managing host files from DSH; no API key or external service is required.
想从 DSH 网页侧栏直接查看运行环境里的目录和文件。
能不能在 Harness 面板里预览文本和图片，再把需要的文件下载下来？
我想从浏览器把文件传到 Harness 所在机器的当前目录。
DSH Host File Explorer 的功能「浏览与预览」：在侧栏打开面板后可跳转目录，查看条目和元数据，并选择文本或图片文件预览内容。
DSH Host File Explorer 的功能「文件传输与建目录」：在面板中下载所选文件、上传本地文件到当前目录，也可填写名称创建子目录。

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds a left-sidebar entry for browsing the filesystem of the machine the Harness runs on.：[](LICENSE) [](#features) [](#architecture) --- Browse the filesystem of the host machine from inside the Harness: directory listings with kinds, sizes, and modification times, text file previews, and folder creation. Every read goes through the Host/Client Remote channel, the same boundary the agent's own filesystem tools use. Files can be downloaded into the browser, and images are previewed inline. Files can be uploaded into the directory that is open.
section: A DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds a left-sidebar entry for browsing the filesystem of the machine the Harness runs on.

text:
@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · Features：| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| File download | Hands the file to the browser through the Harness's authenticated file route, under the file's own name |
| Image preview | Shows a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, or SVG image inline, instead of reading it as text |
| Directory listing | Directories first, then files, each with size and modification time; hidden entries are dimmed |
| Path navigation | Jump to an absolute path, go to the parent, or use the shortcuts for HOME, tmp, cwd, and the filesystem root |
| File preview | Reads the first 256 KiB of a text file and renders it; binary files report themselves instead of printing noise |
| Folder creation | Creates a single-segment subdirectory inside the current directory |
| Multilingual UI | Every visible string goes through `ctx.locale`; the panel ships twelve languages and follows the interface language |
| File upload | Sends a file from the browser to the directory that is open, as one Remote call carrying the bytes |

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · From the plugin market：The plugin is listed in the [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) list, so the marketplace can install it straight from GitHub:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ccfeeling/dsh-host-file-explorer
```

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · As a profile dependency：> **Note**: if your profile has a dependency that ships agent skills (for example `dsh-answer-me-with-html`), pnpm 10.11+ and 12.x refuse to install until the skills directory is declared, and fail with `ERR_PNPM_NO_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR`. Turn off pnpm's own skill linking with one stanza in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
>
> ```yaml
> skills:
>   dirs: []
> ```

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · Architecture：The plugin is a standard DSH bundle with a Host half and a Client half:

```
index.js   (Host)    ctx.hostFiles  ——  seven verbs over node:fs/promises
client.js  (Client)  sidebar entry + main panel + Remote namespace mount
```

The **Host half** provides a `ctx.hostFiles` service and marks its verbs for the Remote transport with the prototype marker `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol/remote-methods`, so the gateway can discover it in SRC mode:

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · Architecture：| Method | Parameters | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `roots()` | — | Well-known locations (HOME, tmp, cwd, filesystem root) |
| `list(path, signal)` | `path` | `{ path, parent, home, entries[{ name, path, kind, size, modified, mime, hidden }], truncated }` |
| `stat(path, signal)` | `path` | `{ path, kind, size, modified, mime }` |
| `read(path, signal)` | `path` | `{ path, size, modified, binary, truncated, text }` |
| `mkdir(path, name, signal)` | `path`, `name` | `{ path }` |
| `upload(path, name, data, signal)` | `path`, `name`, `data` | `{ path, size }` |
| `limits()` | — | The largest file one download may carry |

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · Architecture：`signal` has to be the last parameter: the gateway parses the method signature with `Function.prototype.toString()` to derive the wire parameters, and a broken signature makes the call fail.

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · How files reach the browser：The page never carries file bytes over the Remote channel. It asks the Host for the file's address on the Harness's own authenticated file route — the same route the shipped document preview uses for the images inside a Markdown document — and the browser fetches it with the session the page already holds. A download keeps the file's own name, and a preview gets the file's own content type, so a PNG renders as a PNG.

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · How files reach the browser：One response is bounded by the Harness's attachment byte limit (20 MiB by default). The page reads that number from the Host and refuses an oversized download with an explanation, instead of starting a transfer that would fail.

The **Client half** hand-writes a Typert Remote contribution, mounts it with `ctx.remote.$mount(...)`, and then registers two slots:

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · How files reach the browser：- `sidebar.panellist`: id `host-files`, order `30`, with its own folder icon;
- `main`: key `host-files`, the panel the sidebar button opens.

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · Two traps worth knowing：Shipped plugins can write `inject: ['remote.agentPresets']` only because another package mounts those namespaces, which leaves a consumer free to declare the dependency.

2. **The client half depends on no Harness client package.** This plugin uses `react` and `zod` only, styles itself with `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens, and imports nothing from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` or its siblings.

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · Permissions and boundaries：- The plugin reads the host filesystem with the **privileges of the Harness process itself**: it can read everything the account running it can read. That is inherent to what a host file explorer is, so only enable it on machines and accounts you trust.
- The plugin is **read-only plus folder creation and file uploads**. It cannot modify, delete, or rename a file that is already there, and an upload never replaces one.
- One listing returns at most 2000 entries, and one preview reads at most 256 KiB.
- One download carries at most the Harness's attachment byte limit (20 MiB by default); the panel says so before it starts an oversized transfer.

@local/dsh-host-file-explorer README · Development：```bash
node --check index.js
node --check client.js
npm pack --dry-run      # inspect the file list that actually ships
```

During local development the profile points at the working directory with `link:`, so an edit is live after a browser refresh (the client module is versioned by content hash).
